items.stem: What is a prototype, according to the module?

options.label: A question you can put in front of someone
A small finished product
A written description of an idea

items.hint_text: A prototype exists to answer something.
items.feedback_correct: Yes. A prototype exists to answer a question you can test with a person.
items.feedback_wrong: A prototype exists to answer a question, not to be a mini product or a description. Its job is to test an assumption with a person.

items.stem: You want to learn whether people understand your sign up steps. What is the smallest prototype?

options.label: Clickable screens of only the sign up flow
The full product with accounts and payments
A document describing the sign up idea

items.hint_text: Test only the thing you want to learn about.
items.feedback_correct: Right. Clickable screens of the sign up flow test understanding directly.
items.feedback_wrong: Clickable screens test understanding directly. A full product tests too many things at once, and a document tests nothing a person can do.

items.stem: Which of these are good questions for a prototype to answer? Select all that apply.

options.label: Can a new user finish sign up without help?
Do people understand the main button?
Can the whole company scale next year?
Is the company profitable?

items.hint_text: A prototype answers a small question about how people use it.
items.feedback_correct: Yes. Finishing sign up and understanding the main button are things a prototype can test.
items.feedback_wrong: A prototype answers a small, testable question about how people use it. Scaling or profit are business questions a prototype cannot settle.

items.stem: According to the module, what teaches you more than ten people agreeing with you?

options.label: One person actually using it
A bigger slide deck
A longer written plan

items.hint_text: Agreement is not the same as use.
items.feedback_correct: Correct. One person using the prototype teaches you more than agreement.
items.feedback_wrong: Watching one real person use the prototype reveals problems that agreement never shows. Slides and plans do not put the idea in someone's hands.

items.stem: Which actions count as testing a prototype with a real person? Select all that apply.

options.label: Watch one user try the flow without helping
Ask the user to think aloud
Ask friends if the idea sounds nice
Present the idea in a meeting

items.hint_text: Testing means the person uses it while you observe.
items.feedback_correct: Right. Watching a user try the flow and think aloud is real testing.
items.feedback_wrong: Testing means a person uses the prototype while you observe. Asking if the idea sounds nice or presenting in a meeting collects opinions, not use.

items.stem: Before building a prototype, what should you decide?

options.label: What it has to prove
How polished it will look
How many features it will have

items.hint_text: A prototype is built to answer a question.
items.feedback_correct: Yes. Decide what the prototype must prove before you build it.
items.feedback_wrong: A prototype is built to answer a question, so decide what it must prove first. Polish and feature count matter only after the question is clear.

items.stem: You want to know if people can find the search box. What is the smallest prototype that answers this?

options.label: One screen showing just the search box
The full app with settings and accounts
A slide describing search

items.hint_text: Include only what the question needs.
items.feedback_correct: Correct. Testing findability needs only the screen with the search box.
items.feedback_wrong: Testing findability needs only the screen with the search box. A full app adds unrelated work, and a slide tests nothing people can try.

items.stem: Which prototypes are focused enough to answer one clear question? Select all that apply.

options.label: Clickable screens of just the checkout step
A paper sketch of one screen
The whole product with every feature
A single screen testing the main button

items.hint_text: A focused prototype tests one thing at a time.
items.feedback_correct: Right. One checkout step, one paper screen, and one button test each answer one question.
items.feedback_wrong: A focused prototype tests one thing at a time. The whole product with every feature tries to prove too much at once and hides which part failed.

items.stem: Why show the prototype to one real person instead of many supporters?

options.label: A real user surfaces problems agreement hides
One person is cheaper than many
Supporters are never useful

items.hint_text: Real use reveals what agreement cannot.
items.feedback_correct: Yes. Genuine use reveals problems that friendly agreement never will.
items.feedback_wrong: The value is that genuine use reveals problems that friendly agreement never will. Supporters can still be useful, but they do not replace a real user.

items.stem: You hand your prototype to a person and they get stuck. What is the best next move?

options.label: Watch where they struggled and note it
Explain the answer right away
Decide the prototype is finished

items.hint_text: The struggle is the finding you came for.
items.feedback_correct: Correct. Note where they struggled; that struggle is the finding.
items.feedback_wrong: The struggle is the finding you came for, so record where it happened. Explaining the answer hides the problem, and the prototype is not done until the question is answered.
